source_call_review.summary: Each part of the tool is an upstream call or a line of tutorial code. The tool adds no new scientific computation, duplicates no formula and recomputes nothing.

parts.review: Rebuilds the AnnotationResult that celltypist.annotate returned, from the files written by to_table (classifier.py:188) plus the to_adata h5ad. predicted_labels and majority_voting become 'category' with sorted categories. This is what upstream creates (classifier.py:389 dtype='category'; :498 astype('category')) and it sets the dotplot row order (plot.py:48). Verified: the dotplot tables after the CSV round-trip equal the in-memory dotplot exactly in row order, column order and values, for 13 fixture/prediction/reference combinations. A reversed-category mutant failed 14 tests.

parts.wrapper: celltypist.dotplot(predictions, use_as_reference=reference_key, use_as_prediction=use_as_prediction, return_fig=True); dp.make_figure(); dp.fig.savefig; dp.dot_size_df / dp.dot_color_df .to_csv
parts.review: Direct call with upstream defaults. The tables written are the DotPlot's own attributes, not recomputed. Same figure path as return_fig=False (make_figure), but the DotPlot's own figure is saved instead of pyplot's current one.

Same call. The prediction values come from predicted_labels.csv, which to_adata copies into obs (classifier.py:114), and the indices are checked to be aligned. The tutorial's .loc[['Microglia','Macro_pDC']] becomes the user's reference_groups (selected_groups, nonzero counts); the full table is written to crosstab.csv.

Spying on DataFrame.plot showed the plotted frame exactly equals to_adata(insert_prob=True).obs.loc[group, model.cell_types] from a direct upstream call: same columns in model order, same cell IDs and values. It also equals the executor's boxplot_values_Microglia_Macro_pDC.csv. Only figsize differs, and only when the model has more than 32 cell types.

source_call_review.ignored_parameters: none. All 6 parameters change the output, as the tests show: annotation_dir, reference_key, use_as_prediction, reference_groups, plot_group_probabilities, output_dir. plot_group_probabilities only acts when reference_groups is given, and its schema description says so.
source_call_review.unjustified_restrictions: none found. use_as_prediction is Literal['majority_voting','predicted_labels'], the two values upstream dotplot accepts (plot.py:18-24). The tool requires reference_key to be an obs column. Upstream also accepts an in-memory array, which cannot be passed over MCP. Cell-ID checks (unique; identical order across the three CSVs and the h5ad obs_names; identical decision/probability columns) are needed: _get_fraction_prob_df mixes label-indexed lookups with a positional score list (plot.py:40-42), and duplicate IDs make pred[index] ambiguous. Upstream to_table/to_adata output always passes these checks; the composition test confirms this with the real celltypist_annotate_cells output.
source_call_review.stdout: The tool body runs under contextlib.redirect_stdout(sys.stderr). capfd confirmed no stdout output during a call, and the stdio acceptance run completed the handshake and 9 calls. Observation, not a defect: redirect_stdout is process-wide. Overlapping calls in a threaded server could leave sys.stdout pointing at stderr after both return. This does not affect the MCP stdio transport, which writes to the stdout buffer it captured at startup.
source_call_review.tool_format: Conforms. Every parameter has an Annotated description, closed choices use Literal, the boolean toggle is a bool, and the open-ended group list is list[str]. The two required inputs have no default. The docstring is two lines. The return dict has message, reference (pinned commit URL) and artifacts with absolute paths in a fresh mkdtemp directory per call, plus compact counts. The default base when output_dir is None is <tempfile.gettempdir()>/celltypist_mcp_outputs, the same as the celltypist_tutorial module.
minor_observations: The output subdirectory timestamp format differs from the other module (%Y%m%d_%H%M%S vs %Y%m%d-%H%M%S). Cosmetic.
reference_group_sizes lists every reference group. With very many clusters this field grows, but it holds counts, not arrays.

filter_prediction.implementer_claim: upstream celltypist.dotplot(..., filter_prediction>0) raises KeyError in this environment, so the parameter is not exposed
filter_prediction.independent_reproduction: tmp/verify_celltypist_tutorial_ml/scripts/probe_filter_prediction.py (rc 0, log tmp/verify_celltypist_tutorial_ml/logs/probe_filter_prediction.json). Direct in-memory upstream calls only: celltypist.annotate(demo_500, 'Immune_All_Low.pkl', best match, majority_voting=True), then celltypist.dotplot(pred, use_as_reference='cell_type', use_as_prediction=p, filter_prediction=t), with return_fig True and False, for t in {0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5}.
filter_prediction.result: Reproduced, with a narrower scope than the claim states. Every call where the filter removes at least one predicted label raises KeyError. That was predicted_labels at t=0.05, 0.2 and 0.5, where 29 rows were cut to 20, 11 and 10; both return_fig values failed. Calls where the filter removes nothing succeed: t=0, and majority_voting at every tested t, because all 11 rows have a maximum fraction of at least 0.5. Traceback: celltypist/plot.py:176 sc.pl.DotPlot(...) -> scanpy/plotting/_dotplot.py:219 __init__ -> _prepare_dot_data :330-331 df.loc[order] -> KeyError. The filtered dot_size_df keeps a CategoricalIndex with all 29 categories (11 values, 29 categories at t=0.2), and scanpy reorders by those categories, including the removed ones.
filter_prediction.conclusion: The claim holds for every threshold that actually filters. In this environment (celltypist 1.7.1 at fe357564, scanpy 1.12.4, pandas 3.1.0) filter_prediction only works when it does nothing, so exposing it would not be a repair. Leaving it unexposed is justified. No workaround was added, because one would change the upstream method. It was not used in either tutorial.

boxplot_width.evidence: The DataFrame.plot spy recorded kind='box', rot=90 and title=group, as in the tutorial. figsize was [8.0, 4] for the 10-type custom model (same as the tutorial) and [24.5, 4] for the 98-type Immune_All_Low. The plotted data was exactly the tutorial selection in both cases. Visual check: the 10-type Microglia boxplot matches the executor's reference/figures/custom_seed0_boxplot_Microglia.png (Kupffer cells highest, median about 0.05, outliers 0.66/0.81/0.87). The 98-type Kupffer cells boxplot is legible.
boxplot_width.judgement: Presentation only. Figure size does not affect which values are plotted, the box statistics pandas computes, or the order of cell types. The 32-type threshold and the 0.25 in per type are wrapper choices, not upstream, and do not affect the science.

scientific_comparisons.tolerances: Crosstab counts are compared exactly as integers, with integer dtype asserted. Dotplot fractions and mean probabilities and boxplot probabilities are compared exactly (np.testing.assert_array_equal, tolerance 0); reference values are asserted finite and no nonfinite values occur. Exact comparison is justified because pandas to_csv writes the shortest round-trip float repr (lossless) and upstream applies the same computation to the re-read values. Dotplot fraction columns are also checked to sum to 1 within 1e-12.
scientific_comparisons.ml_cell47: Rows of crosstab.csv for Microglia and Macro_pDC equal, cell for cell over all 11 columns including zeros, the printed DataFrame of executed ml notebook cell 47 (parsed from celltypist_tutorial_ml_execution_final.ipynb) and the executor's crosstab_cell_type_x_majority_voting_Microglia_Macro_pDC.csv. Microglia: Alveolar macrophages 8, DC1 13, Endothelial cells 1, Macrophages 32, Neutrophil-myeloid progenitor 1, pDC 5. Macro_pDC: Alveolar macrophages 5, Macrophages 1, pDC 34. selected_groups equals the nonzero entries (n_cells 60 and 40).
